mechanism: Both drugs are hepatically metabolized and can increase each other's serum concentrations; mefloquine may inhibit sulfamethoxazole metabolism while sulfamethoxazole may displace mefloquine from protein binding, increasing free drug levels and CNS penetration.
action: Monitor for increased sulfamethoxazole toxicity (crystalluria, Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and mefloquine adverse effects (neuropsychiatric symptoms, cardiotoxicity); consider alternative antimalarial if sulfonamide prophylaxis is necessary.
